origins: Some of us were always a little different: in family, school, church, or work. Moves, culture, temperament, or interests can leave us feeling like the one who never quite matches the room. After enough awkward moments, “I don’t fit anywhere” becomes a settled conclusion.
teaches: Paul writes, “We who are many are one body, and each member belongs to one another,” and “God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.” Peter says, “You are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession.” “God settles the lonely in families.” Fitting in and belonging are different. A body needs different parts, and your difference is part of how God designed you to serve others. You belong in His family, and He can lead you to places where you are welcome.
self_statements: I never match the people around me.
I always feel out of place.
There is no group for someone like me.
I have to change who I am to be accepted.
I will always be the odd one.
Everyone else seems to know the rules.
errors: Treating some awkward settings as proof I belong nowhere.
Feeling out of place and concluding I do not belong.
Predicting that I will never find my people.
questions: Where have I felt most like myself, even briefly?
What interests, values, or gifts do I have that could draw like-minded people?
What would belonging, as opposed to fitting in, look like for me?
What do I do to change myself in groups?
How does God see my differences?
Where could I try one new group?
truth: Belonging does not require being the same as everyone else. God made me with a purpose, and He gives me a place in His body. I can look for people and groups where who I am is welcome.
hw_truths: God settles the lonely in families.
log: Each week, note one setting or person where you felt at ease.
actions: List when you felt most yourself.
Visit a class, club, church group, or volunteer opportunity.
Ask one person about their story.
Write how your difference helps the body.
prayer: Father, You made me on purpose. Show me where I belong and the people You have prepared for me. Free me from changing myself to be accepted. Amen.
hw_questions: Where do I feel at ease?
What am I like when I feel most myself?
What do I change in groups?
How does God see my difference?
Who could I ask about their story?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Each member of the body belongs, and I belong too.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I don't fit in anywhere.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
